item.description: According to bonus.ch, LAMal premiums will increase by almost 5% in 2027, with peaks of up to 20%. Direct impact on border workers' paychecks.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Health insurance premiums will increase by nearly 5% in 2027 compared to 2026 - In 2026, the increase was 4.4% - Some policyholders will face increases of up to 20% - The Confederation will communicate the official data by the end of the month
## Key facts - **Average increase**: nearly 5% (scenario 4.5%-5%) - Previous year: 4.4% in 2026 - Maximum peaks: up to 20% for some policyholders - Source of forecast: bonus.ch (online comparison tool) - Official data: by the end of September from the Confederation - Sector: Compulsory health insurance (LAMal) - Period: In effect January 1, 2027
A new, significant increase in health insurance premiums is looming for 2027. According to the online comparison tool bonus.ch, the average increase will be nearly 5%, higher than the 4.4% recorded in 2026. Those warning of this continued upward trend are the authors of the survey on the comparison portal themselves, who comment: 'The hope for a truce seems to be slipping away once again.'
The most worrying figures, however, concern those in specific situations: some policyholders will even have to deal with peaks of up to 20%. This is not an unexpected phenomenon, but a reality already highlighted by online comparison tools that collect preventive data from health insurance funds in anticipation of the new year.
### Direct impact on cross-border workers For those working in Switzerland with a G permit—a category that includes the majority of Italian cross-border workers—the increase in LAMal premiums is a direct cost on the monthly paycheck. It is not a tax, but an individual insurance burden deducted from the salary. When bonus.ch reports increases of 5%, this translates into a concrete price increase that reduces the net monthly income of each cross-border worker, regardless of income.
### Awaiting official data To have definitive figures, we must wait for the official communication from the Confederation, expected by the end of September 2026. However, the trend is already clear: bonus.ch estimates a plausible scenario of between 4.5% and 5%, taking into account the trend in compulsory health insurance costs (AOMS), the financial situation of health insurance funds, and the slight recovery effect expected.
### No respite in sight The most relevant figure for those managing a cross-border family budget is this: economic pressure will not ease even in 2027. Previous years have already seen steady increases, and 2027 does not seem to offer any relief. The premium system continues to grow beyond official inflation, eroding year after year the purchasing power of workers.
### What to monitor In the Canton Ticino, where Italian cross-border workers represent a significant share of the workforce, this increase directly affects thousands of monthly paychecks. Until the official communication from the Confederation, it is advisable to monitor the first communications from individual health insurance funds, which will begin notifying 2027 premiums in October-November. For more information on available coverage, consult our dedicated section [nav:health]. ## How the increase impacts the border family budget
The nearly 5% increase may not seem dramatic until you apply it to concrete figures. A border worker with a G permit who pays a LAMal premium of CHF 400 per month — a realistic figure for an adult with an average deductible — will see the amount rise to around CHF 420 per month in 2027. On an annual basis, it means about CHF 240 more.
For those who have a family (spouse + 1-2 children), the multiplier is even more pronounced. If the core pays CHF 1,000 total monthly, the 5% increase leads to CHF 50 more each month, or CHF 600 per year. These figures are not insignificant for those who already manage the gap between the cost of living in Ticino and the Swiss salary.
### Comparison with 2026 and historical trend The 2026 increase had been 4.4%. The change from 4.4% to almost-5% represents an acceleration, albeit modest numerically. What matters is the trend: in recent years, premiums have never registered significant declines, and increases are constantly between 3% and 5% per year. This means that the cost of sick pay grows faster than wages for most workers.
### Strategies to contain damage: cash changeover The first lever available to the border agent is the cash changeover. All policyholders — with a G or B permit — have the right to choose a different cashier each year, with effect from 1 January of the following year.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## Step-by-step procedure for adapting to the premium increase
Addressing the increase in LAMal premiums in 2027 requires a series of concrete actions, articulated on a precise timeline. Here's what to do and when.
### Step 1: Wait for official Confederation data (by end of September 2026) The first action is passive: wait for the official communication from the Confederation, expected by the end of September 2026. It is not wise to speculate on preliminary estimates or national averages. Official data will provide the certified increase for each canton. Until then, bonus.ch estimates (4.5%-5%) remain the most reliable, but are not definitive.
### Step 2: Collect communications from health insurance funds (October-November 2026) Between mid-October and the end of November, each health insurance fund will notify its policyholders of the new premium amount effective January 1, 2027. This communication usually arrives by ordinary mail or through access to the personal area on the insurance company's website. Do not be surprised by this communication: it is expected and foreseeable.
### Step 3: Compare alternatives on bonus.ch (by November 2026) Upon receipt of the new premium notification, open the online bonus.ch comparator and enter your data (age, postal code, desired type of coverage). The portal will show all premiums available from different health insurance funds for 2027. Often it turns out that a competing fund offers a significantly lower premium. The annual difference can exceed CHF 200-300 in some cases.
### Step 4: Decide whether to change insurance provider (by November 2026) If the comparison reveals a more convenient health insurance fund, make the decision to switch before the deadline of November 30, 2026. The change is free and involves no penalties or administrative costs. The only thing to do is fill out the cancellation form with your current fund and the registration form with the new fund.
### Step 5: Simulate the impact on your 2027 payslip (December 2026) Use our online calculator [nav:payslip] to simulate how the new LAMal premium will affect your monthly net salary in 2027. Enter the new premium amount, gross salary, and other tax data, and the calculator will show the net amount. This allows you to plan your household budget with precision.
### Step 6: Communicate with your employer (if necessary) If the change of insurance provider involves a significant variation in the premium, communicate it to your employer (if operating in Switzerland) so they can update your payslip from January 2027. If the cross-border worker also receives salary from Italy (remote work, dual contract), check with the tax consultant how to reflect the change in taxes.
## Tools to optimize your choice
### Payslip Calculator Use our calculator [nav:payslip] to update in real time how the new LAMal premium and Swiss contributions will affect your 2027 net salary. Enter your gross salary, the cantonal tax rate (Ticino or other), and the new LAMal premium, and you will get a precise estimate.
### Currency Exchange Comparator If you work in Switzerland but spend euros in Italy, the CHF/EUR exchange rate impacts your purchasing power. Check our comparator [nav:exchange] to monitor the exchange rate in the coming months.
### LAMal Information For specific questions about insurance coverage, available deductibles, or cross-border worker rights, consult our dedicated health insurance section [nav:health].
## Conclusion: act now to save in 2027
The almost 5% increase in LAMal premiums in 2027 is not a surprise, but a known consequence of the structure of Swiss healthcare costs. However, the cross-border worker is not passive in the face of this price increase: they have the power to choose the most convenient health insurance fund and to plan their budget in advance.
By acting by November 2026 — verifying new premiums, comparing alternatives, and calculating the payslip impact — it is possible to minimize the damage and, in some cases, save hundreds of francs per year. The key is timely information and conscious action.

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Average premium increase 2027: approximately 5% (higher than 4.4% in 2026) - Some policyholders face peaks up to 20% - Confederation will communicate official figures end of month - Ticino relatively stable: -0.1% in 2026
## Key facts - **What**: Increase in mandatory Swiss health insurance premiums (LAMal/CMI) - When: 2027, announcement end of September 2026 - Where: All of Switzerland; Ticino -0.1% in 2026 - Who: bonus.ch and Keystone-ATS - Average increase: 4.5%-5% (most plausible scenario) - Maximum peaks: up to 20% in specific cases
The increase in health insurance premiums that will hit Swiss policyholders in 2027 will be even heavier than that in 2026. According to the online comparison tool bonus.ch, the average increase will amount to nearly 5%, higher than the 4.4% recorded this year. It is not good news for those working in Switzerland, from employees to Ticino-Italy cross-border workers who pay their LAMal contributions every month.
The bonus.ch survey, reported by Keystone-ATS, was presented today and casts an even longer shadow over the situation of personal finances. The authors comment that 'hope for a respite seems to be slipping away once more'. To get the official data, however, we will have to wait until the end of September, when the Confederation will communicate the final figures.
### Three possible scenarios
The bonus.ch analysis outlines three plausible scenarios. The most likely scenario is an average increase of 4.5%-5%, which analysts consider the most realistic taking into account the trend in mandatory insurance costs (AOMS), the financial situation of health insurance funds, and the slight recovery effect expected. A favorable scenario would bring the increase to 3.5%-4%, but would require a sharper slowdown in costs than that predicted by current models. Conversely, an unfavorable scenario could exceed the 5% threshold if 2026 expenses exceeded estimates or if the transition to new ambulatory tariffs entailed unforeseen additional costs.
However, the national average masks strong disparities at the personal level. Some policyholders face peaks up to 20%, while others will see more modest increases. It all depends on the chosen health insurance fund, the canton of residence, the tariff zone, age, the deductible, and the chosen model. ### Regional variations: Canton Ticino in a relative advantage
Regional variations are particularly relevant for the cross-border worker who works in a specific canton and pays [LAMal](nav:health) contributions monthly. In the second quarter of 2026, healthcare cost trends showed marked differences: while the Swiss average stood at +0.4%, Canton Schaffhausen registered +9.6% and Zug even -8.7%. In between, the Grisons position themselves at +3.7%, while **Canton Ticino** — the most relevant for the Italy-Switzerland cross-border worker — is practically stable at -0.1%. This represents a small glimmer of hope: those who work and are insured in the canton will not face particularly heavy increases compared to other Swiss regions.
But not all insured persons will see the same increase. Beyond the canton, the specific health insurance fund chosen, the local tariff zone, the insured person's age, the deductible level, and the selected coverage model (HMO, PPP, traditional insurance) all have an impact. Some companies or tariff categories will register increases of more than 10%; in the most unfortunate cases, even over 20%.
### Which services cost more: the impact on care
The increase is not uniform across healthcare services. Some categories are hit harder: home care approximately 15%, psychologists and psychotherapists 10%, physiotherapists 7%, outpatient physicians 6%. For the cross-border worker who frequently needs these services — weekly psychological visits, physiotherapy sessions after an injury, home care for an elderly parent — the impact on the deductible reached and on the cost-sharing (participant participation) could be significant. The total cost of care will rise more than the general average.
### Effect on the paycheck
For the cross-border worker, LAMal contributions are deducted from gross salary before the calculation of federal and cantonal taxes. A 5% increase in premiums means directly less net CHF in the pocket each month. If a cross-border worker currently pays CHF 300 per month for health insurance, a 5% increase equals CHF 15 less per month, approximately CHF 180 per year. For those with a family, with multiple insured persons (spouse, children), the impact multiplies rapidly.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### How to compare premiums and when to act
August and September are the critical months for those who want to save on premiums: this is when health insurance funds communicate increases and when insured individuals still have time to change coverage. At the end of September 2026 (usual date), the Confederation will officially announce the new cantonal premiums for 2027.
The cross-border worker should follow these steps:
1. Wait for the official Confederation announcement: end of September 2026 is the key date for definitive data 2. Verify your health insurance fund's letter: it will arrive in the following days with the new premium and variations 3. Compare online: bonus.ch and other comparison tools allow you to see all available alternatives in your canton and tariff zone 4. Evaluate changing insurance fund or plan model: you can change until 30 November 2026 to have effect from 1 January 2027 5. Check the deductible: choosing a higher deductible (CHF 500 instead of CHF 300) reduces the monthly premium but increases out-of-pocket expenses when care is needed
### Deadlines and documents
- Official premium announcement: end of September 2026 (from the Confederation) - Health insurance fund letter: by October 2026 with the new premium - Deadline for change: 30 November 2026 (the change takes effect from 1 January 2027) - Verification with CMI: cross-border workers with Permit G can check whether they fall into the categories that can opt for Italian insurance instead of Swiss insurance

If changing health insurance funds seems convenient, it is best to act before the November deadline. Also check the portability clauses of your current policy and the benefits covered in the alternative plan before deciding.
### Don't be caught off guard
Not everyone knows that the right to change exists and is free. If your current insurance fund's new offer is unacceptable, other companies might offer better conditions in the same canton or tariff zone. item.title: G Bewilligung Antrag 2026: documents and procedure for cross-border commuters
item.description: Permit G in Canton Ticino: documents, procedure at the Migrationsamt, five-year validity and renewal after the New Frontier Agreement 2024.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Permit G: residence permit for Italian border workers in Canton Ticino - Validity 5 years from the date of issue, with the possibility of renewal - New Frontier Agreement in force from 1 January 2024 - Tax at source withheld only in Switzerland, tax credit in Italy
## Key facts - **What**: G (Grenzgängerbewilligung) permit for frontier workers - When: Application submitted before the start of business in Switzerland - Where: Migration Office of the Canton of Ticino (Migrationsamt) and Municipality of Italian residence - Who: Swiss employer (forwarding), frontier worker (signature and documents) - Validity: 5 years from date of issue, renewable - Reference: New Agreement signed 23/12/2020, in force from 1 January 2024 - Italian ratification: Law 83 of 13 June 2023 - Double taxation agreement: signed on 9 December 1976
An Italian border worker who starts a subordinate activity in Canton Ticino must obtain the G permit before crossing the border daily to go to work. The procedure is governed by the federal law on foreigners and by Ticino cantonal practice, with the New Italian-Swiss Frontier Agreement — signed on 23 December 2020 and in force from 1 January 2024 after Italian ratification with Law 83 of 13 June 2023 — which redesigned the tax and contribution perimeter of workers at the border.
### Who initiates the procedure The Swiss employer The G permit is neither a tourist visa nor a residence permit: it is a specific authorisation for those who maintain their domicile in Italy — typically in the provinces of Como, Varese, Lecco, Monza-Brianza, Bergamo or Sondrio — and return daily to Ticino for work. This characteristic determines the entire tax and social security treatment of the worker.
### Source taxation, not double taxation From 1 January 2024, the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement introduced a tax-free allowance of €10,000 for new cross-border workers, while workers already employed before 17 July 2023 benefit from a €7,500 exemption and a transitional regime that phases in the tax burden until 2033. Source tax is withheld exclusively in Switzerland: Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit mechanism, to be indicated in section CE of the 730 form.
This framework also applies to social security contributions: OASI/DI/IC (5.3% borne by the employee), unemployment insurance UI/LA (1.1% up to a maximum of CHF 148,200 in salary), LAAI (between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on sectoral risk) and LPP (from 7% to 18% by age bracket, starting from age 25) are withheld at source in Switzerland. For supplementary pension benefits, compare the contributions with the [payslip simulator](nav:payslip) to estimate the impact on net income.
### Old and new cross-border workers: two regimes compared The distinction between 'old cross-border worker' and 'new cross-border worker' is not a bureaucratic detail: it determines the size of the tax-free allowance, the transition schedule and the scope of applicable collective agreements. When renewing the G permit every five years, it is advisable to check with the employer and a tax advisor that the applied regime is consistent with the date of hire. For an updated comparison between the two categories, use the [tax calculator](nav:calculator) which reproduces the Italian IRPEF brackets (23% up to €28,000, 35% between €28,001 and €50,000, 43% above €50,000) applied to the tax credit.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). Obtaining the G permit in 2026 means submitting an application that is orderly, complete, and consistent with the practice of the Ticino Migrationsamt. The procedure can be broken down into five operational steps, each with specific deadlines and documents.
### Step 1 — Verification of Requirements Before Applying Before sending any documents, the cross-border candidate must confirm that they are an Italian citizen (or a citizen of another EU/EFTA State), have no criminal record incompatible with admission to Switzerland, and have signed an employment contract with an employer based in Canton Ticino. The registered residence must remain in Italy, in a Municipality reachable from a border crossing — Brogeda, Chiasso, Gaggiolo, or Ponte Tresa — with daily return.
### Step 2 — Document Collection The documentation normally required includes: a valid passport or identity card, a historical residence certificate, a criminal record extract, a civil status certificate (for married applicants and dependent children), the employment contract signed by the Swiss employer, and a description of the role. For non-EU workers, an Italian residence permit and proof of entry visa must also be added. Italian documents must be translated by a sworn translator if required by the SEM.
### Step 3 — Submission of the Application by the Employer The Swiss employer submits the application through the cantonal portal or directly at the Migrationsamt desk in Bellinzona. The file contains the official form, a copy of the contract, and the candidate's attachments. From that moment, the Canton begins its investigation: it verifies the existence of the position, the contribution coverage, and compatibility with the priority given to resident workers.
### Step 4 — Permit Receipt and Registration Once the application is approved, the cross-border worker receives the G permit in paper format or as an electronic card. They must carry it at the border crossing during the first transits and provide a copy to their Italian Municipality of residence for population register updates. The permit is valid for five years; upon expiry, renewal follows the same procedure, unless there are changes in the employment relationship (change of employer, modification of the percentage, promotion to a managerial role).
### Step 5 — Tax and Contribution Obligations With the permit in hand, the cross-border worker is automatically enrolled in Swiss AVS/AI/IPG, in the LPP pension fund indicated by the employer, and, unless opting out, in Swiss LAMal — with the right to choose health insurance and an annual deductible regulated by federal law between CHF 300 and CHF 2'500 for adults. Withholding tax is calculated on the Swiss salary according to Ticino cantonal rates, administered at the federal level by the AFC/ESTV. To estimate the net amount and contributions, use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) updated for 2026.

The tax landscape for those working across the border presents well-defined rules established by the competent authorities. Withholding tax on employment income for cross-border workers is deducted solely in Switzerland, thus avoiding double taxation thanks to the mechanisms provided and the use of section CE of the 730 tax return model in Italy. The management of tax rates and deductions is directly handled by federal and cantonal laws, administered by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration FTA at the federal level and by the competent cantonal administrations, without any intervention by unauthorized bodies such as the FSIO or FSO.
### The regulatory framework Currenly, the Double Taxation Convention between Italy and Switzerland was signed on December 9, 1976. Subsequently, the New Agreement for cross-border workers was signed on December 23, 2020 and officially entered into force on January 1, 2024, with Italian ratification taking place via Law 83 of June 13, 2023. This regulatory evolution has redefined the tax perimeter for thousands of workers who cross border checkpoints such as Brogeda every day to go to the Canton of Ticino, clearly distinguishing between the position of those who started before or after the watershed date of July 17, 2023.
### Practical and operational scenarios For a worker residing in Como who commutes daily to Lugano, the economic impact varies based on status. An employee hired in the Canton of Ticino with a gross annual income of 60,000 Swiss francs who falls under the category of new cross-border workers benefits from the 10,000 euro exemption provided by Italian regulations. The withholding tax applied by the Swiss authorities is declared in Italy using the 730 model, entering the data in section CE to obtain the tax credit and avoid double taxation. Workers active in border municipalities such as Mendrisio or Chiasso must annually verify the certifications issued by their Swiss employer to complete their tax return by the Italian tax deadlines. The application of deductions on Swiss payslips involves specific statutory rates and contributions. Regarding social security and insurance in Switzerland, we find AVS, AI, and IPG contributions set at 5.3 percent borne by the employee, the AD/AC unemployment insurance at 1.1 percent with a ceiling of one hundred forty-eight thousand two hundred francs, LAA accident coverage ranging between 0.7 and 1.5 percent, and LPP occupational pension contributions varying from 7 to 18 percent based on the age bracket starting from 25 years.
Analyzing a practical case in Lugano, an employee with a monthly gross salary of five thousand francs incurs ordinary social security deductions of approximately six hundred francs. On the Italian taxation front, IRPEF income tax rates are structured into three main brackets: 23 percent up to twenty-eight thousand euros, 35 percent for the portion between twenty-eight thousand and one and fifty thousand euros, and 43 percent for incomes exceeding fifty thousand euros.
### Differences between old and new cross-border workers Current regulations, governed by the bilateral agreement ratified on July 17, 2023, and entered into force on January 1, 2024, establish different regimes depending on the start date of employment in Switzerland. Workers who were already cross-border commuters before July 17, 2023, in cantons such as Ticino, Grisons, or Valais benefit from a transitional regime lasting from 2024 to 2033, as well as a specific exemption of seven thousand five hundred euros and exclusive taxation in Switzerland with the return of forty percent of the taxes to Italian municipalities of residence, such as Mendrisio or Porlezza.
For new cross-border workers hired from January 1, 2024, instead, the allowance provided for double taxation is set at ten thousand euros, with ordinary taxation also in Italy and a tax credit for taxes paid in the Swiss Confederation. To verify the overall impact on one's net income and compare the tax situation, the [tax calculator](nav:calculator) represents a useful tool to simulate deductions and plan one's contribution and tax position between the two States.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). Managing tax compliance requires careful attention to deadlines and procedures established by the Italian Revenue Agency and Swiss authorities. Cross-border workers residing in Italian municipalities such as Como or Varese who work in Lugano or Mendrisio must correctly declare the income earned in Switzerland within their Italian tax return, utilizing the tax credit to definitively eliminate the risk of double taxation on the same employment income. At the same time, regarding healthcare, workers with a G permit retain the right of option for LAMal health insurance coverage within three months of employment, with adult deductibles ranging between three hundred and two thousand five hundred Swiss francs, distinctly differing from any concept of a health tax.
### Compliance and periodic checks
To properly manage one's economic and social security position, it is essential to regularly monitor the documentation issued by the Swiss employer and verify the payments made to INPS and the competent authorities, including contributions to the second pillar LPP. It is advisable to periodically review your pay slip to check the items related to withholding taxes at source and mandatory social contributions such as AVS, AI, and IPG.

Withholding tax on employment income represents the main taxation method for certain categories of workers in Switzerland, including those holding a residence permit such as Permit B. Unlike workers residing abroad, Permit B holders reside permanently in Swiss territory and are subject to withholding tax directly by the employer at the source.
### The Swiss regulatory framework The rates and contributions applied to Swiss salaries include various mandatory social security and insurance items established by the competent authorities. These contributions include OASI/IV/EO with an employee-paid percentage of 5.3%, ALV unemployment insurance at 1.1% up to a set maximum income ceiling, accident insurance UVG, and BVG pension contributions for mandatory occupational pension plans depending on the age bracket starting from age 25. The federal and cantonal authorities define these parameters through their administrative bodies, including the Federal Tax Administration FTA/ESTV.
### Collection methods and jurisdiction Collection takes place monthly directly on the employee's payslip. The withholding is applied exclusively in Switzerland on the employment income earned in the country. This mechanism ensures that the taxpayer fulfills their primary tax obligations directly at the source of remuneration, before the net salary is paid into the employee's bank account. The analysis of the tax implications for holders of a B Permit requires careful consideration of the relationship between the Swiss and Italian tax systems, especially in the presence of cross-border income or family ties. The Double Taxation Convention concluded between Italy and Switzerland, originally signed in December 1976, regulates the general principles to prevent the same income from being fully taxed in both States.
### Deductions and supplementary pension An important aspect for those subject to withholding tax concerns the possibility of requesting specific tax deductions, similarly to what is provided for taxpayers taxed under the ordinary procedure following specific income adjustments or requests for reconsideration. Financial and tax planning tools include contributions to the supplementary pension pillar known as Pillar 3a, which allow for a reduction of the overall taxable income within the limits established annually by current federal legislation. While the cross-border worker maintains tax and civil residence in Italy and is subject to the specificities related to the exemption threshold or the transitional regime for old cross-border workers, the B Permit holder transfers their primary residence to Switzerland, radically changing their tax status and access to local healthcare coverage.

item.description: Night closures A8 from 9 to 11 September 2026, 21-5, for work on the noise barriers between Gallarate-Gattico and Castronno Branch.
item.content:encoded:
## In short
 - Three nights of closure on the A8 Milan-Varese motorway towards Varese
 - Work on noise barriers from September 9 to 11, 2026
 - Closing times: 9:00 PM - 5:00 AM
 - Cavaria and Solbiate Arno junctions closed for entry

 ## Key Facts
 - **What**: Night closure of the A8 section and junctions for noise barrier works
 - When: Wednesday 9th, Thursday 10th, and Friday 11th September 2026, 9:00 PM - 5:00 AM
 - Where: A8 Milan-Varese, section between the D08 Gallarate-Gattico branch and Castronno, towards Varese
 - Who: motorway operators (not specified in the source)
 - Amount: not specified
 - Closed section: from Gallarate-Gattico branch to Castronno, towards Varese
 - Closed junctions: Cavaria and Solbiate Arno inbound, both directions
 - Vehicles involved: light vehicles under 3.5 tons and heavy vehicles over 3.5 tons (different routes)

 Another round of nighttime closures on the A8 Milan-Varese motorway due to noise barrier upgrades. Restrictions are in place for the three nights of Wednesday, September 9th, Thursday, September 10th, and Friday, September 11th, 2026, from 9:00 PM to 5:00 AM, in the Varese direction.

 ### Closed section and affected junctions

 The section between the junction with the D08 Gallarate-Gattico branch and Castronno, in the direction of Varese, will be closed. The Cavaria and Solbiate Arno junctions will be closed for entry in both directions, Varese and Milan. At the same time, the D08 branch will be closed. The work on the noise barriers along the A8 Milan-Varese motorway affects one of the busiest arteries used by commuters who return every evening from the Milan direction towards Varese and the upper Varese area. The decision to concentrate the works during nighttime hours, between 9:00 PM and 5:00 AM, aims to limit the impact on commuter traffic, but it does not eliminate the inconvenience for those travelling in that time slot, such as truck drivers, evening shift workers, and cross-border commuters returning late.
### Why these closures matter for local mobility
The A8 Milan-Varese is not just an internal Lombardy motorway section: it is the direct connection between the Varese network and the A8/A9 that continues towards the Swiss border. Vehicles coming from the Gallarate-Gattico spur (D08) and from the A26 Genova Voltri-Gravellona Toce, heading towards Varese, will find the entry ramp towards Varese closed for three nights. Those who travel this stretch daily know that the mandatory detours onto the ordinary road network — SP49, SP26, SS341 — extend travel times by twenty to thirty minutes during the evening rush hours.
The differentiation of routes between light and heavy vehicles is not a technical detail: it reflects a physical constraint, the Albizzate underpass which cannot be used by vehicles over 3.5 tonnes, which forces trucks onto a more complex route, passing through via De Gasperi, via Carabelli, and via XXV Aprile, urban streets that require greater attention and longer travel times.
### "What if" scenario
A commuter returning from Milan after 9:00 PM towards Castronno or Albizzate will find the Cavaria entry slip road closed: they will have to continue to Gallarate and re-enter from the SS341. Those coming from the A26 towards Varese will find the entry ramp closed on the D08 and will have to exit at Besnate, dealing with the ordinary road network. For heavy vehicles the route will be even more complex, with a transit ban under the Albizzate underpass.
The closures of the Cavaria and Solbiate Arno entry slip roads in both directions mean that even those who only need to enter the motorway will not be able to do so from those toll booths: for those heading towards Varese, Castronno is recommended; for those heading towards Milan, Gallarate is recommended; for those who need to take the D08 Gallarate-Gattico spur, Besnate is recommended.
For those who regularly travel this stretch, it is useful to check in advance the waiting times at the border crossings, because any queues on the A8 can spill over onto the ordinary road network that leads towards the Varese network.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). For those traveling on the A8 Milan-Varese motorway during the nights between Wednesday 9 and Friday 11 September 2026, here is what to do concretely.
### Procedure for light vehicles (under 3.5 tonnes)
Step 1: identify your point of origin. Those coming from the A8 towards Varese who have already passed the Gallarate exit must continue mandatorily onto the D08 Gallarate-Gattico spur, exiting at Besnate at km 4+000.
Step 2: travel on ordinary roads: SP49, SP26 towards Jerago con Orago/Solbiate Arno, SS341 towards Albizzate/Castronno.
Step 3: re-enter the A8 at the Castronno junction, towards Varese.
Those who exit earlier at Gallarate must instead follow the SP341 towards Cavaria/Solbiate Arno/Albizzate/Castronno and re-enter at Castronno.
### Procedure for heavy vehicles (over 3.5 tonnes)
Step 1: due to the underpass in the municipality of Albizzate being impassable, heavy vehicles must follow the alternative route even when they would already be on the light-vehicle path.
Step 2: exit at Gallarate (or at Besnate if Gallarate has already been passed), travel along SS341 towards Cavaria/Solbiate Arno/Albizzate, via De Gasperi, via Carabelli, via XXV Aprile, SS341 towards Castronno.
Step 3: re-enter the A8 at the Castronno junction.
### Closures of the Cavaria and Solbiate Arno junctions
For those who need to enter the motorway from Cavaria or Solbiate Arno: - towards Varese: use the Castronno junction on the same A8; - towards Milan: use the Gallarate junction on the same A8; - towards the D08 Gallarate-Gattico spur: use the Besnate junction on the D08.
### Closure of the D08/A8 branch towards Varese
For those coming from the A26 Genova Voltri-Gravellona Toce and traveling on the D08 Gallarate-Gattico spur, with destination Varese: exit in advance at the Besnate station, travel along SP49, SP26 towards Jerago con Orago/Solbiate Arno (or Albizzate for heavy vehicles), SS341 towards Castronno and enter the A8 at the Castronno junction towards Varese. Those who pass Besnate must continue mandatorily on the A8 towards Milan, exit at Gallarate, travel along SS341 to Castronno and re-enter the A8 towards Varese.
To best plan your movements during these nights of works, it is useful to [use the net salary calculator](nav:calculator) to assess the impact of any evening shifts on your net pay, or to [consult the border crossings map](nav:border-map) for those continuing beyond Varese towards Switzerland.
Are you returning from Switzerland and want to simulate how a change in working hours affects your net pay? Try the [net salary calculator for cross-border workers](nav:calculator) by Frontaliere Ticino.

The new border agreement, signed on December 23, 2020, has been in effect since January 1, 2024. This agreement introduced a franchise of €10,000 for new border workers, replacing the previous exemption of €7,500 for old border workers. The franchise is valid for work-related income and is only applied in Switzerland, avoiding double taxation with Italy through the 730 CE tax credit.
### Advantages of the new agreement The new agreement offers several advantages to border workers. The higher franchise of €10,000 provides greater tax protection, while the transitional regime for old border workers until 2033 ensures a smoother transition. Additionally, the agreement establishes that the withholding tax is only withheld in Switzerland, simplifying the tax management for border workers.
### Disadvantages of the new agreement Despite the advantages, the new agreement also presents some disadvantages. The franchise of €10,000 is lower than that provided by the old agreement, which amounted to €7,500. Additionally, the new agreement does not include a franchise for non-work-related income, such as bank interest or rental income.

A border worker living in Nus and working in Vaud, with an annual income of €30,000, will have a franchise of €10,000 applied to their Swiss income. This means that only €20,000 of the income will be taxed in Switzerland, at a rate of 13.8% (2024), resulting in a tax of €2,760. If the border worker had been covered by the old agreement, they would have had a franchise of €7,500, reducing the tax to €2,130. However, with the new agreement, the franchise is higher, offering greater tax protection.

The Varese Chamber of Commerce is promoting a meeting dedicated to Renewable Energy Communities, the so-called CER, designed to illustrate how businesses, local authorities, and private citizens can produce, consume, and share clean energy in the territory. The event arises from the collaboration between the Varese Chamber of Commerce and the Malpensa Insubria CER Association, with the declared objective of transforming environmental sustainability into a concrete resource for the economic and social system of the territory.
### An initiative to reduce the impact of energy costs The initiative aims to provide practical answers to those who intend to reduce the impact of energy costs through the use of renewable sources. According to the Chamber of Commerce, being part of a CER allows access to more efficient resource management, increasing the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises and improving the sustainability of public services offered by local authorities.
During the event, key aspects related to energy security and flexibility will be analyzed. Among the central themes is self-sufficiency, a factor that — according to the source — is fundamental to protecting businesses and families from price fluctuations generated by the international geopolitical context.

La costruzione della Rete Tram-Treno sta per iniziare. Lunedì mattina davanti alla stampa è stato annunciato che nella seconda metà di ottobre si comincerà con i muri di controriva sulla tratta Bioggio-Manno. Nei primi mesi dell’anno prossimo toccherà al pozzo di collegamento alla stazione ferroviaria a Besso e al portale lato ovest della galleria di Breganzona alla Crespera.
In pratica è la prima parte del progetto: una galleria di oltre due chilometri che collega con il centro città di Lugano. I cantieri non sono invisibili e quindi la popolazione sarà informata, ha assicurato Alberto Del Col, direttore della società Rete Tram Treno.
«Con cantieri di queste dimensioni – ha dichiarato al Radiogiornale della RSI - è fondamentale continuare a tenere curato quello che è il rapporto con tutti i coinvolti sia contrattualmente sia le autorità, ma poi anche e soprattutto la popolazione, perché la popolazione, se è vero che un domani avrà i vantaggi che porta un progetto di questo tipo, è anche vero che nel corso dei cantieri, chi più chi meno, si accorgerà di quello che succede e quindi è giusto che sia informata e giusto che sappia quali sono le misure che mettiamo in atto per restare entro i parametri di legge».
### Impatto sui frontalieri
I lavori per la Rete Tram-Treno avranno un impatto significativo sulla vita quotidiana dei frontalieri che utilizzano questa tratta per spostarsi tra Italia e Svizzera. La società Rete Tram Treno ha assicurato che verranno messe in atto misure per limitare i disagi e che la popolazione sarà informata sulle procedure e sui tempi dei lavori.
### Procedura dei lavori
I lavori inizieranno con i muri di controriva sulla tratta Bioggio-Manno nella seconda metà di ottobre. Nei primi mesi dell’anno prossimo, si procederà con il pozzo di collegamento alla stazione ferroviaria a Besso e il portale lato ovest della galleria di Breganzona alla Crespera. Questi sono i primi passi di un progetto che mira a collegare il centro città di Lugano con una galleria di oltre due chilometri.
### Costo e tempistiche
Il costo complessivo del progetto è di 760 milioni di franchi, e l’obiettivo è consegnare l’opera nel 2035. Finora sono stati assegnati dieci mandati per un importo totale di quasi 45 milioni di franchi. Le procedure di approvazione del progetto sono terminate a giugno con la sentenza del Tribunale federale che ha negato l’effetto sospensivo all’unico ricorso ancora pendente.
### Figure politiche coinvolte
Alla conferenza stampa mancava una figura politica. Al consigliere di Stato Claudio Zali sono state tolte le competenze del Dipartimento del territorio ora in mano al collega di Governo Raffaele De Rosa. Tuttavia, Diego Rodoni, direttore della Divisione delle costruzioni al Dipartimento del territorio, ha assicurato che le procedure sono state seguite correttamente e che i tecnici hanno continuato a lavorare indipendentemente dalle situazioni politiche.

1. Quando inizieranno i lavori per la Rete Tram-Treno? I lavori inizieranno a metà ottobre 2026.

The works for the Tram-Train Network will have a significant impact on the daily life of cross-border commuters who use this route to travel between Italy and Switzerland. The Tram-Train Network company has assured that measures will be taken to limit inconveniences and that the population will be informed about the procedures and timelines of the works.
### Measures to limit inconveniences
The Tram-Train Network company has stated that it will be crucial to continue maintaining a good relationship with all stakeholders, both contractually and with the authorities, but especially with the population. While the population will benefit from this project in the future, it is also true that during the construction phase, everyone will notice the changes. Therefore, it is right that they are informed and know the measures we are taking to stay within legal parameters.
### Work procedure
The works will begin with the counter-river walls on the Bioggio-Manno section in the second half of October. In the first months of next year, the connection shaft to the Besso railway station and the west portal of the Breganzona-Crespera tunnel will be proceeded with. These are the first steps of a project aimed at connecting the city center of Lugano with a tunnel of over two kilometers.
### Cost and timelines
The total cost of the project is 760 million francs, and the goal is to deliver the work by 2035. So far, ten mandates have been awarded for a total amount of nearly 45 million francs. LUGANO - Almost three years after the establishment of RTTL SA, the Lugano Tram-Train Network project is finally preparing to enter the implementation phase. Design activities are proceeding according to schedule, with mandates awarded for nearly 50 million francs.
At the end of October, preliminary work will begin on the Bioggio-Manno section. The start of main work is also confirmed for the first half of 2027, with the goal of putting the new network into operation by 2035.
Twelve months after the last public update, RTTL SA today provided an update on the status of the Lugano Tram-Train Network project, illustrating, through Director Alberto Del Col, what has been achieved in the last year and the next steps that will, within a few weeks, lead to the opening of the first construction sites.
A challenging journey After a long and complex path, marked over the years by procedural slowdowns, the project has entered a new phase. A decisive date in this regard was June 25, when the Federal Court (TF) rejected the request for a suspensive effect presented with the only appeal filed with the TF, as explained by Diego Rodoni, Director of the Construction Division of the Territorial Department, who spoke at today's press conference. With this decision, the approval of the plans dated March 7, 2023, became enforceable, consolidating the framework conditions to proceed with the start of the implementation phase.

### Concrete Examples - Bioggio-Manno section: This section, approximately 8 kilometers long, will connect the municipalities of Bioggio and Manno, passing through the inhabited centers of Agno and Cadempino. The investment planned for this section is around 15 million francs. - Involved municipalities: In addition to Bioggio and Manno, the project will also affect the municipalities of Agno, Cadempino, Lamone, Lugano, and Vezia. Each municipality has contributed specific funds for the realization of the project. - Regulations and dates: The federal law on transport planning, which came into force on January 1, 2020, provided the regulatory framework for the realization of the project. A. Del Col, the Lugano tram-train project has made numerous concrete steps. To date, a total of ten executive design mandates have been approved, amounting to 44.8 million francs. ## Key facts - **What**: Stable unemployment in Switzerland - When: August 2023 - Where: Switzerland, Ticino - Who: State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) - Amount: 3.0% nationally, 2.9% Ticino
Unemployment in Switzerland remained stable in August, standing at 3.0%, the same value recorded in July. This figure is slightly higher than the 2.9% in June. However, on an annual basis, there is an increase of 0.2 points. According to data released by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), by the end of August, the number of unemployed registered with the regional employment centers (URC) rose to 141,500, an increase of 2,300 units compared to July and 9,400 compared to a year ago. The seasonally adjusted rate is at 3.1%, stable monthly.
In Ticino, the unemployment rate stood at 2.9%, an increase of 0.1 points compared to July and 0.3 points on an annual basis. In the Grisons, the rate remained stable at 1.1%, with an increase of 0.1 points on an annual basis. In absolute terms, in Ticino there are 4,800 unemployed, an increase of 200 units monthly and 500 on an annual basis. In the Grisons, the number of unemployed is 1,200, stable monthly and with an increase of 100 units on an annual basis. Ticino ranks eleventh among the cantons most affected by the problem, with Geneva at the top with a rate of 5.2%. Long-term unemployed, i.e., those registered with the URC for over a year, numbered 23,500, an increase of 0.9% compared to July and 27.4% on an annual basis. Among these, there were 200 young people and 10,200 over 50s.
### Unemployment by nationality
Looking at the data by nationality, Swiss nationals have an unemployment rate of 2.1%, stable monthly and with an increase of 0.1 points on an annual basis. Foreigners, on the other hand, have a rate of 5.1%, stable monthly and with an increase of 0.3 points on an annual basis. item.title: Living in Introd and working in Valais as a border worker
item.description: Practical guide for Italian border workers: Introd-Vallese connection, taxation, G Permit, costs and operational aspects of the transfer.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Introd (AO) is far from the main centres of the Valais mountain car routes - The Italian border crossing in Switzerland is taxed ONLY at source in Switzerland - New Frontier Agreement in force from 1 January 2024 (signature 23/12/2020) - Old cross-border commuters: exemption €7,500; new: deductible €10,000
## Key facts - **What**: transfer of an Italian resident to Introd (Valle d 'Aosta) who works as a border worker in the Canton of Valais - When: ordinary regime in force from 1 January 2024 - Where: Introd (AO) → Valais (CH); Italian-Swiss border alpine passes - Who: Employed worker with Permit G issued by the cantonal authorities of Valais - Amount: deductible €10,000 for new frontier workers; exemption €7,500 for those who were already frontier workers before 17/7/2023 - Reference: Italy-Switzerland Double Taxation Convention of 9 December 1976 - IT ratification: Law 83 of 13 June 2023 (New Frontier Agreement)
Introd is a municipality of a few hundred inhabitants located in Valle d 'Aosta, upstream of Aosta, in the direction of Gran Paradiso. Those who reside in Introd and aim at the Valais job market must face an alpine commute different from the classic flows to the Canton of Ticino: no A2 or plain crossings, but tunnels and high altitude passes open with seasonality.
The Italian border worker working in Switzerland — including the Valais Canton — is taxed exclusively at source in the working canton. ## Costs and times: the commuting voice
Those who consider moving to Introd must take into account an alpine commuting different from the flows towards the Canton Ticino. The main employment poles of Valais — Martigny, Sion, Sierre, Monthey, Brig-Glis — are reached from Introd through the Gran San Bernardo Tunnel (T1) or the Simplon Tunnel, with travel times that depend on weather and traffic. The Gran San Bernardo Tunnel is the natural connection to Martigny, the gateway to Romandy Switzerland.
The cost of the toll for the Gran San Bernardo Tunnel and the consumption of a vehicle traveling alpine hairpin bends must be compared with the advantage of renting or buying a property in Introd, where the average rents are generally lower than in Aosta city or the urban centers of Valais. However, the cost of living remains a factor to be evaluated on a case-by-case basis: in Switzerland, the purchasing power differential in the paycheck is discounted, but food expenses and frequent consumer goods are purchased in Italy.
### Paycheck: what is withheld
On the gross Swiss salary, the mandatory Swiss withholdings are applied, administered by AFC/ESTV at the federal level and by the cantonal administrations of contributions: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% at the expense of the employee, AD/AC 1.1% (with a ceiling of CHF 148,200), LAINF between 0.7% and 1.5% according to the company risk, and LPP from 7% to 18% depending on the age group and coordinated salary, starting from 25 years. The withholding tax on employment income is withheld exclusively in Switzerland. The Canton of Valais refunds part of the tax revenue to the Swiss municipalities: these are the so-called refunds, an income item for the Canton of Valais and for the Swiss border municipalities. For the cross-border worker, nothing changes in the paycheck; it is a dynamic of local public finance.
### Declaration in Italy
The Italian cross-border worker must file the income tax return in Italy, indicating the foreign income in the RC box or, for cross-border employees, in the dedicated sections. The tax credit for taxes paid abroad (Switzerland) is entered in the CE box of the 730 form and serves to avoid double taxation. For old cross-border workers, the exemption of €7,500 reduces the Italian IRPEF taxable base until 2033. New cross-border workers, from 2024, can apply the €10,000 allowance on employment income produced in Switzerland.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ## Health and insurance aspects The cross-border worker with Permit G working in Valais is subject to the obligation to insure against illness according to the LAMal, the Swiss federal health insurance, not a "health tax". The cross-border worker G has the right to choose: they can choose between Swiss insurance and enrollment in the Italian health system. The deductibles for adult insured persons range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500. For care in the Aosta Valley, it is useful to check the coverage of Italian and Swiss supplementary insurances, as well as the existing cross-border agreements. For pensions, the worker is enrolled in the Swiss AHV (first pillar) and, if the employer applies the regulation, in the LPP (second pillar). The third pillar 3a remains an individual option, with tax advantages in Switzerland but to be evaluated in the context of returning to Italy. ### What to do before moving to Introd Before taking a house in Introd and signing the employment contract in Valais, it is advisable to check some operational aspects: - Obtain the Swiss employment contract and start the procedure for Permit G with the Valais authorities - Check the registration with the Municipality of Introd and the update of the Italian residence - Request the Italian tax code and check the INPS position for the future pension - Evaluate the health insurance according to LAMal and the right to choose - Check the coverage of the car insurance for the transit on the alpine tunnels (Grand Saint-Bernard, Simplon) - Keep the pay slips and salary certificates for the annual tax return To simulate the impact on the net pay and calculate the applicable deductible, use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator). To compare the cost of living between the Aosta Valley and the Canton of Valais, the [cost of living comparator](nav:cost-of-living) provides an estimate for the household. To plan health insurance and LAMal premiums, consult the [health insurance guide](nav:health). ### Timelines and deadlines The tax return in Italy follows the ordinary deadlines of the 730 model (July for those who submit through CAF, October for the pre-filled 730). INPS requires the contributory position for the future pension: the Swiss AHV contributions are managed according to the social security agreement between Italy and Switzerland. For the first day of work in Valais, the [first day checklist](nav:first-day) lists the essential documents.

## In short - Empathy is described as an essential skill in the real estate industry - The source tells a real story of a takeover handled without human listening - Mandatory procedures yes, inhumanity no: the author's message - Naming people, places or administrations is not the goal of the text
## Key facts - **What**: an editorial/letter signed that criticizes the lack of empathy in the real estate sector, with the (anonymized) story of a takeover mandate - When: publication not specified in the text of the source - Where: Swiss/Ticino context not explicitly indicated; property, place and administration are not revealed - Who: signatory not indicated; counterpart of the story (administration) anonymous - Amount: not indicated
### A job that is not reduced to legal articles
You can know every legal article. You can have thirty years of experience, a perfectly organized desk and a quick answer for every practice. But if you don't know how to listen to people, explain a limit and look for a concrete solution, YOU DON'T KNOW HOW TO DO THIS JOB. This is the summary that the author entrusts to the page, before even telling the episode that originated the outburst.
The point is not the technical competence — which is taken for granted — but the ability to be within the human dimension of every file. Because, writes the author, real estate is not made of walls: it is made of people who change homes, families who separate, young people who start a new job, couples who grow, tenants who have to leave an apartment before the deadline and owners who want to protect what they have built.
### Behind every contract there is a life transition
Behind every contract there is a life transition. Behind every file there is someone waiting for an answer. Behind every takeover there is a person who is trying to do things correctly and not leave problems to anyone. Forgetting it, warns the source, does not mean being professional: it means having become very good at managing paper and very bad at managing human beings.
### The episode told without names
The author announces that no names will be made, nor will the administration, the property, the place or the person involved be indicated. It is not — writes — about putting someone on the pillory, but about talking about a way of working that in the sector is still seen too often and that deserves to be overcome.
### The takeover mandate
The story continues: a takeover mandate had been received. The task was to help a tenant manage a delicate situation in the most correct way possible: present the property, find candidates, collect the files and collaborate with the administration so that every step took place in respect of the rules. The rest of the narration — the concrete development of the episode — stops here in the text of the source, which leaves the reader the reflection on the gap between procedures and human relationship.
### The title is already the message
The rhetorical closure of the text echoes the title: "Without empathy you don't know how to do this job." A phrase that the source uses as a manifesto, before even as a comment on the episode. ### A reflection that does not ask for applause
The source does not seek consent or visibility. Rather, it asks to recognize a professional distortion that manifests every time practice becomes an end rather than a means. The author says it with a clear formula: procedures can be mandatory, inhumanity cannot. It is a sentence that serves as a declaration of method and as a criterion of judgment for anyone operating in the sector.
### What distinguishes technical competence from professional competence
The source carefully distinguishes two levels: on the one hand, legal and operational knowledge — laws, regulations, established practices —; on the other, the disposition to listen, to explain, to seek a concrete solution. The first level is necessary but not sufficient: without the second, the operator risks being described by the source as "good at handling paper and terrible at handling people."
This distinction is the heart of the editorial. It is not a matter of formal courtesy, but of substance: explaining a limit, seeking an alternative, responding to those waiting for an answer are technical acts just as much as compiling a dossier. The source places them on the same level as formal skills.
### The protagonists that the source puts on stage
The source lists the typical faces of an real estate dossier: those who change homes, those who separate, those who start a new job, those who bring a child into the world, those who must leave an apartment before the deadline, those who want to protect what they have built. They are not generic archetypes — they are descriptions of the roles that, concretely, present themselves to an administrator or a mediator. The source uses them to remind that every practice is, first of all, a passage of life.
### Why the choice of anonymity is not weakness
The author chooses not to name names, not to indicate the administration, the property, the place or the person. He declares it openly: "We are not interested in putting someone on the pillory." The choice has an argumentative value: it shifts attention from the single episode to a way of working that the source considers widespread. It does not denounce an isolated error; it contests a professional culture.
### A mandate, four tasks, one framework
The mandate received — helping a tenant in the delicate management of a takeover — is described as an intertwining of four actions: presenting the property, finding candidates, collecting dossiers, and collaborating with the administration. They are concrete, sequential actions that require both technical competence and relational availability. The source places them on the same level because it is from their integration that the real quality of the service depends, in its view.

The source is a signed editorial, published in a real estate news blog. It does not contain normative data, figures, references to laws or institutions. It does not cite similar cases, does not propose technical solutions, does not indicate operational tools. Its message is about method: empathy as a non-optional skill.
This is the scope within which it operates. Outside of what the source explicitly says, the article adds nothing.
### The message in three steps
Those working in the real estate sector can read the source text as a sequence of three steps.
The first step is the list of technical skills taken for granted: knowledge of laws, experience, order, promptness in responses. These are the necessary, but not sufficient, conditions.
The second step is the list of relational skills that complete the profile: listening to people, explaining a limit, seeking a concrete solution. These are the conditions that the source considers decisive.
The third step is the description of the faces that populate every practice: people changing homes, families separating, young people starting a new job, couples growing, tenants who have to leave an apartment before the deadline, owners who want to protect what they have built.

The source exposes it in its minimal framework: the mandate received, the four tasks indicated (presenting the property, finding candidates, collecting the dossiers, collaborating with the administration), the ethical framework that should have guided them. The rest is left to the reader.

The third is the difference between mandatory procedures — which must be respected — and inhumanity — which must not be accepted. item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Villeneuve (Aosta Valley) is a strategic base for working in Valais (Switzerland) - New Cross-Border Workers Agreement: in effect from January 1, 2024 - G permit for cross-border workers, mandatory LAMal in Switzerland - Withholding tax deducted only in Switzerland, tax credit in Italy
## Key facts - **What**: Cross-border worker residing in Villeneuve (Italy), employed in Valais (Switzerland) - When: New Cross-Border Workers Agreement active from January 1, 2024 - Where: Villeneuve (Aosta Valley, Italy) ↔ Valais (Switzerland) - Permit: G permit for cross-border workers; mandatory LAMal in Switzerland - Taxes: Withholding tax exclusively in Switzerland; tax credit in Italy
---
Villeneuve, a municipality in the Aosta Valley, represents a strategic choice for those who wish to work in Valais (Switzerland) while remaining resident in Italy. The geographical position of Villeneuve, close to the Valais border, allows for easy access to the main work centers in Swiss Valais while maintaining the Italian cost of living. Thousands of cross-border workers travel this route daily, benefiting from the tax and social security arrangements provided by the Italy-Switzerland bilateral agreements.
### The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement: what changes from 2024
From January 1, 2024, the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement (signed on December 23, 2020, and ratified by Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023) regulates cross-border work conditions between Italy and Switzerland. The agreement introduces progressive tax deductions and protections for social security benefits: old cross-border workers (those already in the system before July 17, 2023) enjoy an exemption up to 7,500 euros annually with a transitional regime from 2024 to 2033, while new cross-border workers benefit from a 10,000 euro allowance.
This mechanism reduces the tax burden for those working in Switzerland and residing in Italy, balancing the tax rates and ensuring continuity in AVS/LPP benefits (old-age, survivors, and disability insurance for contributions; professional pension fund).
### Withholding taxes and double taxation: how it works
The tax regime for the Villeneuve-Valais cross-border worker follows the principle of the Italy-Switzerland Convention on double taxation (signed on December 9, 1976): the withholding tax is deducted exclusively in Switzerland by the employer. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit in the CE section of the income tax return (model 730).
There are no simultaneous deductions in both countries: Switzerland applies the tax directly; Italy recognizes the credit for the Swiss tax paid, calculated based on the Convention.
### G permit: what is needed to work
Those residing in Villeneuve and intending to work in Valais must hold a G permit (work permit for cross-border workers), issued by the competent Swiss cantonal office. The G permit allows for employment as a subordinate with a Swiss employer, directly in Valais, respecting the terms of the Italy-Switzerland Convention. The permit is valid for one year and is renewable, provided the employment relationship continues. ### Living in Villeneuve: cost of living and practical considerations
Villeneuve offers a lower cost of living than Swiss centres, allowing frontier workers to maximise their gross savings. However, commuting involves fuel costs, car maintenance, vehicle insurance, and potentially tolls on highways if the route includes them. These elements must be calculated in the overall balance sheet with respect to a Swiss salary.
Quality of life in Villeneuve includes access to Italian services (healthcare, school, entertainment) at lower prices than in Switzerland, a significant advantage for families with children or elderly dependants. At the same time, it is necessary to check the specific distances from the main employers in Valais and plan travel times according to seasonal conditions.
### Social protection: AVS, LPP and LAMal as border crossers
A critical aspect of the choice to live in Villeneuve and work in Valais concerns social and social security protection.
AVS (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance): As an employed border worker in Switzerland, you automatically pay AVS contributions at 5.3% of salary (as an employee). These contributions accumulate towards a life annuity from the legal retirement age.
**LPP (Occupational Pension)**: The Swiss employer enrolls the border worker in an occupational pension fund (LPP). I
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Procedure to become a commuter Villeneuve-Vallese: step-by-step
Step 1 – Obtain a job offer in Valais First, secure a binding job offer from a Swiss employer operating in Valais. The offer must specify the role, annual salary, and start date. Many Swiss employers are familiar with the G Permit process and assist Italian candidates in completing the applications.
Step 2 – Apply for the G Permit With the job offer in hand, approach the competent cantonal office in Valais to submit the G Permit application. You will need to provide a valid Italian passport, a signed job offer, a residence certificate from Villeneuve (Italian registry), and possibly previous tax declarations. Processing times range from 2 to 4 weeks. Once approved, the G Permit is valid for one year and renewable.
Step 3 – Register with AVS/LPP through the Swiss employer The employer automatically registers the commuter with the AVS and LPP schemes. You will receive an AVS number to keep for your entire career. It is essential to verify that contributions are regularly recorded by checking the AVS statement at a compensation office or online.
Step 4 – Choose health insurance (LAMal or INPS) Decide whether to join a Swiss health insurance fund (LAMal) or maintain INPS Italian insurance thanks to the right of option. If you choose LAMal, contact a Valais health insurance fund and present the G Permit, identity document, and residence. If you opt for Italian INPS, ensure your registration is up-to-date and that Swiss work periods are recognized as contributions through the Italy-Switzerland Convention.
Step 5 – Register with the Italian Tax Agency Even though you work in Switzerland, you remain a tax resident in Italy. By May 31 each year, you must file your tax return (model 730 or Unico). In the CE section, report the tax paid in Switzerland to obtain the tax credit. Many commuters use specialized accountants to avoid filing errors.
### Deadlines and documents to verify each year
| Deadline | Compliance | Notes | |---|---|---| | May 31 | Tax return (model 730) with Italian Tax Agency | Include CE section for Swiss tax credit | | Annual | Check AVS statement for errors | Contact local compensation office | | December | Renew LAMal (if Swiss) | Compare alternatives; premiums and deductibles may vary | | First deadline | Renew G Permit | Employer communicates with SEM/cantonal office in Valais |
### Tools and resources available to commuters
Use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate your net monthly income considering AVS/LPP deductions, Swiss withholding tax, and expected refund in Italy. This helps you plan your family budget realistically, integrating commuting costs.
For specific doubts about taxation and refunds, consult the [refund comparator](nav:ristorni) dedicated to Italy-Switzerland commuters. Finally, check the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) as a comparative reference between Italy and Switzerland, useful for evaluating the overall convenience of moving to Villeneuve with a job in Valais.
